name: Orbweaver v1.0.3
body:
**Orbweaver 1.0.3 fixes three things 1.0.2 got wrong on the orbs themselves: dropped orbs that wouldn't stay put, name bubbles and button rings that flickered or stuck open, and chat messages that were typed into a terminal but never sent.** Nothing else has changed since 1.0.2.

## What's fixed

- **A dragged orb now stays where you drop it.** In 1.0.2, an orb you'd never moved before slid back to the stack on the right edge of the screen as soon as you let go, and so did an orb you dragged out of a group or a team lead dragged with its team. How long you held the button made no difference. The second drag of the same orb usually worked, so it could look like the trick was to hold on longer. The first drop now sticks. In arranged mode, and for a group lead dropped next to its own group, the orb still springs back into its slot, as before.
- **Name bubbles no longer flicker across your orbs.** An orb that missed the moment the pointer left it went on acting as if the pointer were still over it, and several such orbs took turns showing their name bubble many times a second, with your mouse nowhere near them. Each orb now checks where the pointer really is, and only one bubble is open at a time.
- **Button rings and usage cards close when you move away.** The same fault left an orb's ring of buttons, or an account orb's usage card, open on orbs you had only brushed past. Sometimes eight or more stayed up until you started a drag. They now close as soon as the pointer is really off them, and only open for the orb the pointer is on.
- **Messages from the chat panel are now sent, not just typed.** Sending to a session running in iTerm2 or Terminal.app on macOS, or in a console window on Windows, put any single-line message longer than about 70 characters into the prompt without submitting it, so you had to switch over and press Return yourself. Codex sessions failed at even shorter lengths, and very long messages could arrive split in two. In kitty and WezTerm, messages were never submitted at any length. All of these now send every message as a single paste and submit it.

## Upgrading

Install over 1.0.2 as usual. Nothing to change.

- **macOS:** as with every upgrade, re-grant Local Network in System Settings → Privacy & Security if your other machines or OpenClaw stop connecting.

## Known limitations

- We fixed the flicker by checking the real pointer position. We still don't know why macOS sometimes fails to tell an orb that the pointer left. The fix doesn't depend on the answer.
- The chat panel fix was measured against one version each of Claude Code and Codex. Terminals reached through tmux were already working and are unchanged.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `Orbweaver-1.0.3-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `Orbweaver-1.0.3-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `Orbweaver-1.0.3-win-x64-setup.exe` |

The `OrbweaverSpeech-*.zip` files are the optional neural speech engine. The app downloads the one it needs, so you don't need to.

name: Orbweaver v1.0.2
body:
**Orbweaver 1.0.2 fixes sessions that went missing on your other machines.** It contains this one fix and nothing else since 1.0.1.

## What's fixed

- **Your other machines now see sessions from every Claude Code profile you've set up.** Orbweaver only offered sessions from the accounts it had listed back when Remote Control was removed. A profile added afterwards under **Settings → Claude Code** was never shared with your other machines. If all of a machine's sessions ran under that profile, the others saw nothing from it, and nothing said why. All of your configured Claude Code profiles are shared now. A profile you add is picked up within seconds, without a restart.
- **Settings now tells you when sessions aren't being shared.** If a machine has live sessions under a folder it isn't sharing, **Settings → Other machines** says so in one line and tells you where to add that folder. The line appears once another machine is connected.

## Upgrading

Install over 1.0.1 as usual. You don't need to change anything: profiles you already added under Settings → Claude Code are shared as soon as the new version starts.

- **macOS:** as with every upgrade, re-grant Local Network in System Settings → Privacy & Security if your other machines or OpenClaw stop connecting.

## Known limitations

- The Settings line only updates while another machine is connected.
- A profile folder that can't be read is recorded in the diagnostic log, not shown in Settings.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `Orbweaver-1.0.2-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `Orbweaver-1.0.2-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `Orbweaver-1.0.2-win-x64-setup.exe` |

The `OrbweaverSpeech-*.zip` files are the optional neural speech engine. The app downloads the one it needs, so you don't need to.

name: Orbweaver v0.5.11-beta
body:
**Claude Buddy is now Orbweaver.** This is the first release under the new name. The app, installers, data folder, hook scripts and speech engine are all renamed, and an upgrade carries your settings across from Claude Buddy automatically. This release also adds orbs for Claude Code sessions hosted by Claude Desktop, and a one-click fix for chat messages Claude Code holds back. It includes a round of reliability fixes too, the biggest of which is for Windows hooks.

## New

- **The rename.** The app is `Orbweaver.app` on macOS and Orbweaver in the Start Menu on Windows. On first launch, your settings and logs move from the old `ClaudeBuddy` folder to an `Orbweaver` one. Hooks are rewired under their new names, and the old ones are removed. Sessions that were already running when you upgraded keep showing up while they finish.
- **Orbs for Claude Code sessions hosted by Claude Desktop.** Desktop's own Claude Code sessions get orbs like terminal sessions do. Their chat panel can send into a Desktop chat bridged over Remote Control.
- **Chat messages that Claude Code held back now have a one-click fix.** When a session runs without permission prompts, Claude Code holds a message from Orbweaver until someone approves it in that session, so chatting from the orb seemed to do nothing. The chat panel now says why, and offers **Let orbs message sessions directly**. Confirm it once and Orbweaver turns on Claude Code's `crossSessionInbound` setting for you, after backing up your `settings.json`. You can then send the held message again without retyping it. The same switch is in **Settings → Claude Code**, where you can also turn it back off.
- **Ending a background job's orb stops the job** through its daemon, instead of leaving it running.
- **The turn-finished voice summary is capped at three sentences**, and it's billed to the account the session runs under.

## Fixed

- **Windows hooks no longer hang on long transcript lines.**
- **macOS stops asking for keychain access over and over.** Credentials are cached, and an unexpired cached login keeps being used when the keychain's timestamp changes.
- **Adding a Claude Code profile says so when its hooks couldn't be wired**, instead of failing silently. The old `--auto-color` flag is no longer passed.
- **The New chat dialog no longer warns "no hooks" on Windows machines that are wired.**

Behind the scenes there's more test hardening on both platforms, including a chat-panel test that could deadlock under coverage.

## Upgrading from Claude Buddy

Install Orbweaver over Claude Buddy as usual. You don't need to uninstall first.

- **macOS: re-grant Automation and Local Network.** Installing replaces `Claude Buddy.app` with `Orbweaver.app` and moves the old app to the Trash on first launch. macOS doesn't carry either permission over to the new app. Without Automation, click-to-focus stops working. Without Local Network, nothing on your LAN can be reached, such as an OpenClaw gateway or a remote-control peer. Re-grant both in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
- **macOS: re-add Orbweaver to Login Items** if Claude Buddy was in them.
- **Codex will ask you to review its hooks again**, because their file changed. Codex runs no hook until you accept.
- **Windows:** the installer removes the old Start Menu group and Startup shortcut.
- If you go back to Claude Buddy, it runs on a snapshot of your settings. Settings you change while downgraded don't carry forward when you upgrade again.

## Known limitations

- The one-click chat fix for held messages applies to sessions on this machine. It isn't offered for a far machine's sessions over the peer link, or for Claude Desktop sessions over Remote Control. Whether Claude Code on Windows can take messages this way at all hasn't been confirmed. The Settings switch works on both platforms.
- A per-user Windows install adds no firewall rule for the peer link, because that needs admin rights. Windows asks the first time Orbweaver listens.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `Orbweaver-0.5.11-beta-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `Orbweaver-0.5.11-beta-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `Orbweaver-0.5.11-beta-win-x64-setup.exe` |

The `OrbweaverSpeech-*.zip` files are the optional neural speech engine. The app downloads the one it needs, so you don't need to.
